text:
Maya: Heads-up — ACME (tenant-47) opened a ticket: svc.acme.internal resolves NXDOMAIN from their tenant VPC after they applied a tightened egress allowlist. Works from other VPCs. They also reported intermittent TLS certs for the public domain. Ticket #12345

Sam: Ok. Do we have their dig +trace from their VPC and from our control plane? Need both to compare.

Maya: Pasting what the customer ran from an instance in their tenant VPC:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> +short svc.acme.internal
;; global options: +cmd

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; SERVER: 169.254.169.253#53(169.254.169.253) (UDP)
```

Maya: And from our control plane in us-east-1:
```
$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @10.0.2.2
10.10.12.34
```

Alex: That smells like split-horizon / duplicate hosted zone. Can you list their private hosted zones and VPC associations? Command we ask customers to run: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?ends_with(Name, `\"svc.acme.internal.\"`)]'` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z3ACMEPRIV`

Maya: Customer returned two hosted zones that both look similar. One is private: Z3ACMEPRIV (assoc with tenant VPC) and another private by mistake: Z9DUPLICATE (assoc with their central mgmt VPC). They had previously attached the duplicate during a migration but didn't remove it.

Jess: If two private zones with the same name exist in different accounts/VPCs, depending on resolver priority and where the query escapes to, you can get inconsistent answers. Do we know their resolver setup (forwarder vs shared resolver)?

Maya: They use a node-local cache + customer NAT to the outbound resolver 203.0.113.58. They mentioned they recently tightened the egress allowlist to a single IP 203.0.113.55.

Sam: Aha — likely their traffic is being SNAT'd to a different egress IP than they allowed, so some flows hit the central mgmt VPC resolver (Z9DUPLICATE) which returns NXDOMAIN, and others hit the tenant VPC resolver which returns the internal A record.

Alex: Also check resolver rule priority / outbound forwarder config. If the resolver in their mgmt VPC has a rule returning NXDOMAIN for that zone, and traffic from some hosts is routed there, that explains the flip.

Maya: Customer posted traceroute to our resolver: 
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.58 (203.0.113.58), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  ip-10-0-0-1.ec2.internal (10.0.0.1)  0.123 ms  0.089 ms  0.080 ms
 2  nat-gw (10.0.0.2)  0.63 ms  0.56 ms  0.49 ms
 3  egress-nat (203.0.113.58)  1.2 ms  1.0 ms  0.9 ms
```

Sam: Confirmed — NAT IP is 203.0.113.58 not 203.0.113.55. If their allowlist only has .55, some queries fail when SNAT picks .58 (or vice versa).

Maya: They also showed `openssl s_client -connect svc.acme.internal:443 -servername svc.acme.internal -showcerts` and sometimes the cert CN is `*.external.acme.com`. So traffic sometimes hits the public ALB.

Alex: That fits — when DNS resolves to the public IP (due to the duplicate hosted zone resolving to public), the TLS handshake shows public cert. When it resolves to internal ENI IP, internal cert is served.

Sam: Repro plan: 1) Ask customer to `dig @169.254.169.253 svc.acme.internal +short` and `dig @10.0.2.2 svc.acme.internal +short` from the same host to see divergence. 2) Check `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` for duplicates. 3) Verify VPC associations: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z3ACMEPRIV` 4) Verify NAT translation IPs vs egress allowlist. 5) If duplicate zone existed, recommend removing the unintended hosted zone or disassociating the wrong VPC.

Maya: I asked them to run the two digs and to `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` — they confirmed the duplicate zone was created by a script earlier. They removed Z9DUPLICATE from their account and reassociated Z3ACMEPRIV to the tenant VPC.

infra-bot: route53-sync job completed: sync hosted zones -> tenant-47 (job id: r53-sync-2026-03-17-15:12) :white_check_mark:

Maya: After removal, customer re-ran dig from the same host: `dig @169.254.169.253 svc.acme.internal +short` -> `10.10.12.34` and TLS cert now shows internal CN. They also expanded egress allowlist to include full NAT pool (203.0.113.0/24) to prevent future SNAT mismatch.

Jess: Great. Any follow-ups for us? Docs or automation to prevent duplicate private zones?

Alex: We should add a one-off warning in tenant onboarding: check for duplicate private hosted zones across mgmt accounts. Also suggest automated CI check that flags new private hosted zone creations with existing zone name matches.

Maya: I'll update the ticket and leave for 24h verification from customer before closing. Leaving repro steps and commands in the ticket.

Sam: Thanks — nice catch.

Maya: marking pending customer verification. :clock1:
